resources.string: Shows the week as a grid of hours, like the day view, instead of a list of days.
Writes the number of the week at the start of each row of the month.
Adds the place, the call link, the repeat and the calendar name under each event in the lists.
Writes the time on the line of now and makes it pulse gently in the day view.
A touch on an empty hour of the day view starts a new event at that hour. Off: only the + button does.
Adds a page with the twelve months of the year. Touch a month to go to it.
On a tablet or an unfolded phone the month and the agenda of the day sit side by side.
Shows the guests of an event and lets you answer an invitation. Off: events show no guests.
A second touch on the day that is already chosen opens its day view.
The form of a new event offers a repeat (every day, week, month, year). Off: new events do not repeat.
Swiping the day view goes to the next or the previous day. Off by default because it can clash with the swipe between pages.
Leaves out of the lists the events you answered no to.
Shows the birthdays of your contacts in the calendar. It needs the permission to read contacts.
A long press on an event of the day view lets you drag it to another hour. It changes the event in your calendar.
Colours the days of the month by how busy they are, from empty to full.
The day view puts each calendar in a column of its own.
Bigger type in the calendar only, without changing the text size of the phone.
Softens the colours of events at night, so they are less bright on a dark screen.
Draws the charts with a grid and shows the exact value when you touch a bar, with a small movement as they draw.
Shows the icon of each app in the lists of use. Off: names only, a little lighter.
The charts take the accent colour of the launcher. Off: the fixed colours that tell Wi-Fi and mobile apart.
Shorter rows in the lists of apps, so more of them fit on the screen.
On a wide screen the lists and the charts go in two columns.
Adds the trend, the projection to the end of the cycle and the signs of unusual use.
Adds a search box and a filter by type of network to the lists of apps.
Shortcuts to the screens of Android that free up space: cache, large files, storage settings.
Does not count the time the launcher itself is on screen in the screen time.
Reads the battery and the network again every few seconds while the page is open. It uses a little battery.
Keeps its own history of use, space and battery on this phone only, beyond what Android remembers.
Looks for the largest files and for duplicates, reading the photos, videos and music you already allowed.
Lets you write the price of your plan and shows what you pay over the limit.
Adds charts by calendar, by hour and the flow from app to network.
Adds a first page with tiles that sum up data, battery and space.
Bubbles with day separators, grouped by sender, links you can touch and the tick of delivery. Failed messages turn red.
Shows the photo or the initial of each contact in the list and in the title of a conversation.
The list follows the messages of the phone as they come in, without pressing refresh. Off: it updates when you reopen it.
On a wide screen the list and the open conversation sit side by side.
Chips with short answers above the box where you write.
Asks the network to tell you when each message arrived. It can cost one more small message with some plans.
A Copy button in the notification of a message with a one-time code.
Lets you block a number from the long press menu: its messages are kept but not told.
Shows the text of a message in the notification on the lock screen too. Off: only \"new message\".
A button to pause a recording and go on from the same point.
A button that puts a marker in the recording, to find a moment again while recording and playing.
A call that comes in holds the recording instead of leaving a gap.
Writes the recording in small frames so that a crash does not lose it. Experimental: it needs a little more storage.
A meter that shows the volume while you record, with the peak.
A control to play at a slower or faster speed.
A bar to move through the recording and buttons to jump ten seconds.
Buttons to move the cut by one second, for a precise trim.
Lets you cut recordings in other formats; they are written again as AAC.
Louder, fade, remove silences, and send as WAV or Opus.
A view that draws the sound by frequency over time.
Keeps the written text of a recording after you leave. Off: it is lost when you close the page. The text stays on the phone.
A short summary of the written text of a recording.
Lets you tag recordings with labels and filter the list by them.
Copies each recording to a folder you choose. You pick the folder when you turn it on.
The record button is round and big. Off: a button across the screen.
Each row of the list also tells the length, the size and the format.
Writes dates as words (yesterday, Monday 3) instead of numbers.
Groups the list under the day of each recording.
An animation between the list and the recording that opens.
A small player under the list to play without opening a recording.
The picture of the wave takes the look of the launcher. Off: a fixed look.
On a wide screen the list and the open recording sit side by side.
A stronger picture of the wave, for easier reading.
Opening the recorder (from its tile too) starts a recording at once, with one touch. The notification of the recording shows as always. Off by default.
While a recording runs, the volume keys put a marker at that moment and do not change the volume (needs markers on). Off by default.

A touch on a headline opens the article in a reading page of the app: only the text and the main pictures, no ads, at the text size you choose. The page is read only when you open the headline. Pictures follow the pictures option of the app. Off: the headline opens in the browser.
